_note: Every value is quoted from the cited source (checked against the PDF/HTML on 2026-10-29). None was re-measured. 'peer_reviewed' is false for arXiv preprints. Values are NOT comparable with BenchFuzz-on-PicoRV32 measurements except where 'comparable_with_benchfuzz' says so.

ChipFuzzer.citation: Wang et al., When Fuzzing Meets Understanding: LLM-Driven Semantic Test Generation for RTL Verification, arXiv:2607.10340v1, 11 Jul 2026

encarsia_bugs_detected.source: Sec. 5.3, Sec. 5.4, Fig. 8 (per-design counts read from the figure labels; they sum to the stated rates)

ChipFuzzer.plateau_rule: cumulative condition-coverage gain < 0.1% over 100 consecutive validated testcases (Sec. 5.1)

Cascade.citation: Solt, Ceesay-Seitz, Razavi, Cascade: CPU Fuzzing via Intricate Program Generation, USENIX Security 2024
Cascade.headline: same coverage 28.2x faster than TheHuzz and 97x faster than DifuzzRTL; 37 new bugs (29 CVEs) in 5 of 6 designs

picorv32_bugs.P1: Accessing a non-implemented CSR causes the CPU to hang (CVE-2023-34898)
picorv32_bugs.P2: Spurious exceptions when reading mandatory CSRs (CVE-2023-34897)
picorv32_bugs.P4: Performance counters can only be read using some opcodes (CVE-2023-34914)
picorv32_bugs.P6: Spurious exception when decoding fence instructions (CVE-2023-34899)

Cascade.source: Sec. 1, Sec. 7 (coverage), Table 4 (bug list), Appendix (DUT commits)
Cascade.comparable_with_benchfuzz: P6 only: same DUT commit f00a88c, reproduced by BenchFuzz (E0 P6 probe and blind fuzzing)

TheHuzz.citation: Kande et al., TheHuzz: Instruction Fuzzing of Processors Using Golden-Reference Models for Finding Software-Exploitable Vulnerabilities, USENIX Security 2022
TheHuzz.headline: reaches coverage 1.98x faster than random regression and 3.33x faster than DifuzzRTL; 11 bugs (8 new)

TurboFuzz.citation: TurboFuzz: FPGA Accelerated Hardware Fuzzing for Processor Agile Verification, arXiv:2509.10400v2, 3 Feb 2026
TurboFuzz.platform: Fidus Sidewinder, AMD Zynq UltraScale+ XCZU19EG, Rocket at 100 MHz
TurboFuzz.headline: up to 2.23x more coverage than software fuzzers in the same time; up to 571x faster detection of real-world issues
TurboFuzz.coverage_vs_cascade: 1.26x-1.31x at 1, 2 and 4 h (Sec. VII-F); vs DifuzzRTL 1.64x-2.23x
TurboFuzz.comparable_with_benchfuzz: throughput order of magnitude only (different DUT and harness)

BMCFuzz.citation: BMCFuzz: Hybrid Verification of Processors by Synergistic Integration of Bound Model Checking and Fuzzing (IEEE, 2025)
BMCFuzz.note: Only the figures reported by ChipFuzzer were retrievable (Table 2, Fig. 8, Sec. 5.4); the primary paper's own numbers were not accessible.

Encarsia.citation: Bolcskei, Solt, Ceesay-Seitz, Razavi, Encarsia: Evaluating CPU Fuzzers via Automatic Bug Injection, USENIX Security 2025
Encarsia.corpus_as_used_by_chipfuzzer: 90 injected bugs, 30 per design (RocketCore, BOOM, CVA6)
Encarsia.comparable_with_benchfuzz: no (different designs); our 15-bug PicoRV32 suite follows the same 'one bug per design copy, detection = ISA-visible divergence' protocol
